defense_in_depth_findings.title: Validator does not pin informational provenance fields of the banked evidence
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: validate_f017_representative_m1f0_concrete_route_values_v1.py pins every consumed route value (selected IDs, routing weights, byte serializations, per-pair IEEE-754 bit patterns, ranking hash, route hash, producer hash, producer output hash, reproduction bundle hash) against constants and recomputation, but does not verify the document fields reconstruction.execution_candidate_sha256, reconstruction.accepted_reproduction_producer_sha256, reconstruction.accepted_oracle_source_sha256, routing_weights.exact_sum, or the historical values in surface_separation.direct_dprefix_selected_ids; mutations of these fields pass validation and are not covered by the mutation tests. This review independently confirmed each of these fields against committed repository bytes (candidate 7c315fc5..., reproduction producer b17f1034..., oracle source ec9a679b..., historical direct-DPREFIX order [250,10,237,73,62,177,218,28] in f017-selected-routing-weight-qualification-v1.json and f017-dprefix-route-ambiguity-v31-evaluation-v1.json), so the fields are currently accurate.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_fix: In a future validator revision, pin execution_candidate_sha256, accepted_reproduction_producer_sha256, and accepted_oracle_source_sha256 to the committed files by rehashing them, require exact_sum == 2.5 as a field check, and pin direct_dprefix_selected_ids to the historical committed route; extend the mutation tests accordingly.
defense_in_depth_findings.justification_for_remaining_open: All load-bearing route values consumed by future expert recovery are hash-pinned and mutation-tested; the unpinned fields are provenance annotations independently enforced by the recovery producer at run time and verified against committed artifacts in this review.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Expert input activation remains hash-only in the repository
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The banked concrete route values cover the ordered top-8 expert IDs and binary64 routing weights, which is the complete route input for preparing representative expert recovery. The actual expert input activation (router_normalized, stage hash 687a692a..., derived from post_attention_residual 8309377e...) remains hash-only in committed evidence. It is deterministically reproducible from the retained release-1 payloads plus the four retained point authorities with zero checkpoint rereads (demonstrated 10/10 in the banked reproduction bundle and re-demonstrated live in this review), but no committed artifact yet names it as a required future expert-recovery input.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_fix: The future representative expert-recovery authorization must explicitly bind the expert input activation as a first-class input, either as banked concrete bytes or as a retained-only derivation bound to stage hash 687a692a452e30860c34055942061f4ff368ec0e1c815439c71e457a444fe62c, rather than leaving it implicit.
defense_in_depth_findings.justification_for_remaining_open: The reviewed sufficiency question is preparation of expert recovery, not execution; preparation requires only the ID-keyed selected experts and routing weights, which are banked concretely, and the activation derivation path is proven retained-only and deterministic.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Recovery producer does not pin the candidate hash at invocation
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: f017_representative_m1f0_recover_route_values_from_retention_v1.py accepts any --candidate path and records sha_file(candidate) in its output without enforcing the expected constant 7c315fc5... . A wrong candidate cannot alter the result because every packed payload hash, decoded identity, stage hash, selected-ID hash, weight hash, ranking hash, and route hash is enforced against constants bound to the banked real execution, and the deterministic output identity 3dadd8fe... transitively pins the candidate; but the failure mode would surface as a downstream identity error instead of an immediate candidate-identity rejection.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_fix: Add an EXPECTED_CANDIDATE_SHA256 constant check at the top of recover() in any future revision of the producer.
defense_in_depth_findings.justification_for_remaining_open: The producer output was byte-identically reproduced in this review using the committed candidate; all consumed values are transitively pinned, so the missing check affects only error-reporting ergonomics, not integrity.

statement: I independently reviewed cycle 1 of the F017 representative M1-F0 route-authority loop at exact HEAD b81a18f4eb280e384a8a2742ee35554fa5d9d8c9 with a clean tree, using repository bytes as the sole authority. I verified the retained release-1 package identity by rehashing all machine-local payloads and state records against the banked receipts, re-executed the committed retained-only recovery producer and reproduced its declared output byte-for-byte including all nineteen stage hashes, and independently recomputed the uint16 LE selected-ID serialization, the binary64 LE weight serialization, and the canonical route hash in pure Python, all matching the banked values a0f2e2b5..., ff1a7127..., and 03dc2dfb... derived from the single nine-read real event dc53b458.... The review consumed zero checkpoint reads, zero shard opens, and zero expert executions, and left the ledger at 175. No blocking or non-blocking-required findings exist; three defense-in-depth findings remain open with explicit justification. The banked concrete route values are sufficient to prepare, but not execute, representative expert recovery. Verdict: ACCEPT.
